provenance.source: Existing local imagegen front derived from the reviewed V8 reference sheet
provenance.hiddenSurfaces: Inferred by the reconstruction; no back or side images were supplied
provenance.parameters: Same V8 Hunyuan3D-2mv settings: seed 1412, steps 10, guidance 5, octree resolution 256

reviewEvidence.method: Visual inspection of actual gray GLB renders, comparison with approved V2 six-view source and V8 renders; no mesh editing or topology instrumentation

hair.outcome: Limited local change; principal defect remains
observations: V9 appears to have fewer prominent long detached needle-like pieces and a somewhat more contiguous outer hair mass than V8. This is a qualitative render comparison, not a measured component-count reduction.
Both profiles and the back remain a broad curtain-like mass with shredded sheets, ridges and ragged edges. V9 does not recover the source's coherent smooth layered curls.
Top and bottom views expose dense rough relief across the hair mass; detached-looking fragments remain visible in front, back and three-quarter renders.

limbs.outcome: Small front-view improvement, insufficient for production
observations: Legs remain visibly separate; the front hand silhouettes have somewhat more readable finger protrusions than V8's short mitten-like ends.
Hands still show short/fused-looking digits and rough wrist/cuff boundaries. Visual inspection cannot certify finger topology or skin deformation.
Source sneaker lacing, layered sole and collar shapes remain softened into generic rounded forms.

clothes.outcome: Changed coat panel silhouette, no fidelity pass
observations: V9 front lower coat panels are less broad and rounded than V8, but panel edges, lapels and cuffs remain lumpy or ragged.
Shirt, belt and hardware relief is irregular and does not reproduce the crisp source layering.

density.interpretation: Higher face count has not resolved the visible shape defects.

blockingDefects.observation: Broad curtain-like hair silhouette with noisy shredded surface instead of smooth coherent tied hair and layered curling locks in the approved source.
blockingDefects.implication: Hair must be reconstructed or rebuilt; smoothing and removing floaters alone cannot supply the missing source-like lock shapes.

blockingDefects.observation: The low fringe and ragged material around the cheeks/neck obscure or flatten the intended eye/face region; the approved source leaves the large eyes and face clear.
blockingDefects.implication: Head and fringe shape need correction before identity can be accepted.

blockingDefects.observation: Irregular lapel/panel/cuff boundaries and stubby fused-looking finger relief remain.
blockingDefects.implication: Silhouette and usable hand/garment boundaries require shape work before rigging or texture baking.

nonBlockingObservations: Headphone band and earcups, separate legs, shorts and a body-only standing silhouette remain recognizable.
No suitcase or floor/base geometry is apparent in the seven renders. This is a visual observation, not a full disconnected-component inventory.
materialAndProductionRisks: No texture is present in the reviewed renders. Blue eyes, lavender hair, black/gold clothing, stars and material fidelity have not been validated.
Dense ragged hair and garment relief could produce noisy normals, shadows and texture bakes if transferred to a production asset.
Front-only inference leaves the back, scalp/ponytail construction and hidden clothing uncertain despite the available approved six-view comparison.
The wide hair mass may cause animation clearance problems; no rig, skin weights, UV layout or deformation were reviewed.
1,098,020 triangles requires a later topology/asset-budget pass after the shape is corrected. No production budget was established by this review.
Manifoldness, exact connectivity and component counts were not independently tested.
nextAction: Preserve as a front-only diagnostic. Compare a genuinely different reconstruction or rebuild hair/head/garment shapes from the approved views before retopology, rigging or texture approval.
furtherSmoothingReason: One cleanup can remove local floaters but does not address the curtain silhouette, missing coherent curls or face/garment shape errors. A further smoothing-only pass is unlikely to change the gate.
